blocks.text: Two coils are placed close together (Fig 17.20). One, connected to a battery through a switch S and a rheostat, is the primary coil; the other, connected to a galvanometer, is the secondary coil. If the current in the primary is changed by varying the rheostat, the magnetic flux in the surrounding region changes. Since the secondary is in the magnetic field of the primary, the changing flux also links the secondary, and an emf is induced in it.

blocks.title: Mutual induction
blocks.text: Mutual induction is the phenomenon in which a changing current in one coil induces an emf in another coil.

blocks.alt: A primary coil, connected through a switch and a battery to a rheostat with current Ip, stands end to end with a secondary coil joined to a galvanometer, current Is. Magnetic field lines pass from the primary through the secondary.
blocks.caption: Figure 17.20: Circuit diagram to find Mutual induction between two coils (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 17.20).

blocks.text: By Faraday's law, the emf in the secondary is es = -Ns d(phis)/dt (17.39), where Ns is the number of turns in the secondary. The net flux through the secondary, Ns phis, is proportional to the magnetic field of the primary current, which is proportional to Ip: Ns phis = M Ip (17.40), so M = Ns phis / Ip, where M is the mutual inductance of the two coils.

items: The number of turns of both the primary and secondary coils.
The area of cross-section of the two coils.
The magnetic permeability of the medium between the coils.
The nature of the material on which the two coils are wound.
The distance between the two coils.
The orientation of the primary and secondary coils.

blocks.text: Using equation 17.40, es = -d(Ns phis)/dt = -d(M Ip)/dt, so es = -M dIp/dt (17.41). The emf in the secondary is proportional to the rate of change of current in the primary, and the negative sign shows that it opposes the change in the primary current. The magnitude of the mutual inductance is M = es / (dIp/dt) (17.42).

blocks.title: Mutual inductance and the henry
blocks.text: Mutual inductance is the ratio of the average emf induced in the secondary to the time rate of change of current in the primary. Its SI unit is V s A^-1, the henry (after Joseph Henry): one henry is the mutual inductance of a pair of coils in which a rate of change of current of one ampere per second in the primary induces an emf of one volt in the secondary.
Mutual inductance is used in transformers, electric motors and generators, plays a part in signal processing, and is used in devices such as pacemakers and metal detectors.

blocks.title: Brain teaser: how does a pacemaker work?
blocks.text: Do you have an idea how a pacemaker works? A pacemaker sits under the skin of the chest, with pacemaker leads running into the right atrium and right ventricle of the heart.
